Sam (support): hi @Amelia — saw your ticket about the generator dropping answers and 401s after the region switch. can you paste the request headers you sent?
Amelia (customer): pasted below. this started around 16:05 UTC. tokens spiked on our bill and results became very short. we send region: us-west in our header but responses show eu-west in logs. curl included.
Amelia (customer): ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" -H "X-Client-Region: us-west-2" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"rwd-llm-3b", "prompt":"Summarize...", "max_tokens":512}'```
Sam (support): thanks. attaching the request_id you sent?
Amelia (customer): request_id: r-20260304-8a1c. stack traces: 401s for a subset of calls, others returned a short one-paragraph summary instead of full output.
Elena (infra): quick check in ingress logs for r-20260304-8a1c — incoming hits the us-west ELB, but routing service logged a policy mismatch and forwarded to eu-west pool at 16:05:27 UTC. grabbing linked deploys.
Marta (routing): that sounds like the new route-priority patch we rolled yesterday. if a preferred pool is saturated we fall back to region-standby candidates. curious why it chose eu-west given X-Client-Region=us-west-2 — maybe misread header name.
Raj (ml-eng): note: eu-west standby pools run rwd-llm-3b-quantized-v1 (reduced vocab mapping) — tokenizer differences can truncate outputs or drop special tokens. that explains short outputs.
Sam (support): ok that's our hypothesis: header mismatch -> cross-region fallback -> incompatible quantized variant served -> capability gap + some auth 401s. can we confirm a header parsing bug?
Marta (routing): found the routing log excerpt: ```[16:05:27] req=r-20260304-8a1c headers={"x-client-region":"us-west-2", "x-region":"us-west"} selected_pool=eu-west-standby reason="header_pref_match_failed"``` looks like we canonicalize to lower-case but expect "x-region" not "x-client-region". new patch normalized header keys but didn't include the alias.
Elena (infra): deploy-bot shows a canary config pushed 2026-03-04T15:58:00Z that changed header alias list: deploy-bot: "config/routing: add header_aliases=[x-region,x-region-id] removed x-client-region"
deploy-bot: <config deployment id: cfg-6732, by: marta>
Raj (ml-eng): action item: need immediate mitigation for customers — ensure fallback pools use compatible model variants or prevent cross-region routing that picks quantized backfills.
Sam (support): telling Amelia: temporary workaround: add header "X-Region: us-west" to requests. also we've escalated for a hotfix.
Amelia (customer): adding X-Region works, thanks. will monitor token usage. can you confirm we won't be billed for truncated runs because of misroute?
Elena (infra): billing team notified. tagging billing@ — we'll scope runs after we have logs for r-20260304-8a1c and adjacent ids.
Marta (routing): immediate tasks: revert header alias change OR re-add x-client-region alias + safety check to avoid serving quantized-standby for production contracts. scheduling hotfix now. ETA 45m.
Raj (ml-eng): also pushing update to standby pool mappings: mark quantized variants as "capability_degraded" so routing can prefer fallback that preserves tokenizer compatibility.
Sam (support): thanks everyone. Amelia, I'll follow up in this thread with the billing outcome and the hotfix rollout times. :thumbsup:
Amelia (customer): appreciate the quick help. :pray:
